RGPD-A5.title: Principles relating to processing
RGPD-A5.statement: Base each processing operation on the six core principles and be able to demonstrate compliance with them at any time. This last point, accountability, turns a principle into a burden of proof: it is not for the regulator to establish the breach, but for the organisation to establish its compliance.

requirements.RGPD-A5-R1: Process data lawfully, fairly and transparently in relation to the data subject.
requirements.RGPD-A5-R2: Collect for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes, and not process further in an incompatible way.
requirements.RGPD-A5-R3: Limit data to what is adequate, relevant and strictly necessary (minimisation).
requirements.RGPD-A5-R4: Keep data accurate and up to date, and erase or rectify inaccurate data without delay.
requirements.RGPD-A5-R5: Set and apply retention periods limited to the purpose pursued.
requirements.RGPD-A5-R6: Ensure integrity and confidentiality through appropriate technical and organisational measures.
requirements.RGPD-A5-R7: Build and maintain the evidence needed to demonstrate compliance with all these principles.

RGPD-A5.deadline: Ongoing requirement, enforceable at any time
evidence: Data protection policy approved by management
Retention policy and retention schedule by data category
Records of periodic review of processing

RGPD-A6.title: Lawfulness of processing
RGPD-A6.statement: Identify, for each processing operation, one of the six legal bases, document it and apply it consistently. A legal basis cannot be switched during processing to regularise after the fact.

requirements.RGPD-A6-R1: Assign a single, explicit legal basis to each processing purpose.
requirements.RGPD-A6-R2: Document the balancing test when the basis is legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)).
requirements.RGPD-A6-R3: Check that any further processing is compatible with the original purpose (Art. 6(4)).

RGPD-A6.deadline: To be established before each processing starts
evidence: Record of processing stating the legal basis

RGPD-A7.title: Conditions for consent
RGPD-A7.statement: Where processing relies on consent, be able to show that the person consented, present the request in a distinguishable and intelligible way, and make withdrawal as easy as giving consent.

requirements.RGPD-A7-R1: Keep proof of consent: timestamp, scope, version of the text shown.
requirements.RGPD-A7-R2: Present the consent request separately from other terms, in clear and plain language.
requirements.RGPD-A7-R3: Offer a withdrawal mechanism as easy as the collection mechanism.

evidence: Screenshots of consent collection and withdrawal interfaces

RGPD-A9.title: Processing of special categories of data
RGPD-A9.statement: Processing sensitive data is prohibited in principle. It only becomes possible under one of the ten exhaustively listed exceptions, which must be identified and documented in addition to the Article 6 legal basis.

requirements.RGPD-A9-R1: List processing involving health, biometric or genetic data, or data revealing origin, opinions, beliefs, trade union membership, sex life or sexual orientation.
requirements.RGPD-A9-R2: Identify for each the Article 9(2) exception relied on, in addition to the Article 6 basis.
requirements.RGPD-A9-R3: Strengthen security measures in proportion to the sensitivity of the data.

evidence: Justification of the exception relied on

RGPD-A12-14.chapter: Chapter III: Rights of the data subject
RGPD-A12-14.title: Transparency and information to individuals
RGPD-A12-14.statement: Inform individuals at the time of collection, or within a month when data is obtained indirectly, with concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible information.

requirements.RGPD-A12-R1: Provide the controller's identity, purposes, legal bases, recipients, retention periods and rights.
requirements.RGPD-A12-R2: Inform at the time of direct collection, or within one month at most for indirect collection (Art. 14(3)).
requirements.RGPD-A12-R3: Mention transfers outside the Union and the related safeguards where relevant.

RGPD-A12-14.deadline: At collection, or within one month for indirect collection

RGPD-A15-22.chapter: Chapter III: Rights of the data subject
RGPD-A15-22.title: Exercise of data subject rights
RGPD-A15-22.statement: Set up a procedure to answer requests for access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection within one month, extendable by two months for complex requests.

requirements.RGPD-A15-R1: Publish a channel for receiving requests and log every request received.
requirements.RGPD-A15-R2: Verify the requester's identity without collecting excessive data.
requirements.RGPD-A15-R3: Reply within one month, extendable by two months with a reasoned notice to the person.
requirements.RGPD-A15-R4: Provide portable data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format (Art. 20).
requirements.RGPD-A15-R5: Frame automated individual decisions and provide for human intervention (Art. 22).

RGPD-A15-22.deadline: One month from receipt, extendable by two months
evidence: Log of requests and response times
guidance: Responding to a subject access request

RGPD-A24.title: Responsibility of the controller
RGPD-A24.statement: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and demonstrate compliance, and review and update them where necessary. This is the governance foundation from which the record, impact assessments and internal policies flow.

requirements.RGPD-A24-R1: Define an internal data protection policy approved at management level.
requirements.RGPD-A24-R2: Assign identified data protection roles and responsibilities.
requirements.RGPD-A24-R3: Review and update the measures at a defined frequency.

RGPD-A25.title: Data protection by design and by default
RGPD-A25.statement: Build data protection safeguards into processing from the design stage, and ensure that by default only the data needed for each purpose is processed, in volume, extent, retention period and accessibility.

requirements.RGPD-A25-R1: Build a data protection checkpoint into the project life cycle.
requirements.RGPD-A25-R2: Apply the most protective configuration by default: minimisation, short retention, restricted access.
requirements.RGPD-A25-R3: Use pseudonymisation and minimisation from the design stage where the purpose allows.

RGPD-A25.deadline: At each design or redesign of a processing operation
evidence: Data protection milestone in the project methodology

RGPD-A26.title: Joint controllers
RGPD-A26.statement: Where two entities jointly determine purposes and means, set out by agreement how obligations are shared, notably the exercise of rights and information to individuals, and make the essence of it available to data subjects.

requirements.RGPD-A26-R2: Formalise a joint controllership agreement allocating obligations.
requirements.RGPD-A26-R3: Publish the essence of this agreement for data subjects.

RGPD-A27.title: Representatives of organisations not established in the Union
RGPD-A27.statement: An organisation not established in the Union but subject to the regulation under Article 3(2) must designate in writing a representative in the Union, in one of the Member States where the data subjects are.

requirements.RGPD-A27-R1: Designate in writing a representative established in the Union.
requirements.RGPD-A27-R2: Mention this representative in the information given to data subjects.

RGPD-A27.deadline: As soon as processing falls under Article 3(2)
conditions: Organisation not established in the Union

RGPD-A28.title: Contracts with processors
RGPD-A28.statement: Only use processors providing sufficient guarantees, and govern the relationship with a written contract containing the eight mandatory terms of Article 28(3). Missing clauses are among the most frequent findings in inspections.

requirements.RGPD-A28-R1: Assess the processor's guarantees before contracting.
requirements.RGPD-A28-R2: Set out in the contract the subject matter, duration, nature, purpose, data types and categories of data subjects.
requirements.RGPD-A28-R3: Provide for documented instructions, confidentiality, security, assistance, deletion at the end of the contract and audit.
requirements.RGPD-A28-R4: Frame sub-processing with written authorisation and flow-down of the same obligations.

RGPD-A28.deadline: Before any processing is entrusted to a third party
guidance: Guidelines 07/2020 on the concepts of controller and processor

RGPD-A30.title: Records of processing activities
RGPD-A30.statement: Keep a written record of all processing activities and make it available to the supervisory authority on request. The exemption for organisations with fewer than 250 employees is in practice ineffective as soon as there is a risk, non-occasional processing or sensitive data.

requirements.RGPD-A30-R1: List each activity with purposes, categories of data subjects and data, recipients and retention periods.
requirements.RGPD-A30-R2: Mention transfers to third countries and the applicable safeguards.
requirements.RGPD-A30-R3: Describe in general terms the security measures applied to each processing operation.
RGPD-A30-R4: Keep a separate record for processing carried out on behalf of third parties.
If the organisation acts as a processor

RGPD-A30.deadline: Record kept up to date at all times
evidence: Record of processing carried out as a processor

RGPD-A32.title: Security of processing
RGPD-A32.statement: Implement technical and organisational measures ensuring a level of security appropriate to the risk, and have a process for regularly testing and evaluating their effectiveness. This is the article that overlaps most directly with NIS2 and DORA.

requirements.RGPD-A32-R1: Implement pseudonymisation and encryption of data where appropriate.
requirements.RGPD-A32-R2: Ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of systems and services.
requirements.RGPD-A32-R3: Be able to restore availability of and access to data in a timely manner after an incident.
requirements.RGPD-A32-R4: Regularly test, assess and evaluate the effectiveness of the measures.
requirements.RGPD-A32-R5: Ensure that anyone acting under authority only processes data on instructions.

RGPD-A33.title: Notification of a breach to the supervisory authority
RGPD-A33.statement: Notify the supervisory authority of any personal data breach within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to rights and freedoms. Every breach, notified or not, must be documented internally.

requirements.RGPD-A33-R1: Have a breach qualification procedure and an identified point of contact.
requirements.RGPD-A33-R2: Notify the authority within 72 hours, or justify any delay.
requirements.RGPD-A33-R3: For a processor: alert the controller without undue delay.
requirements.RGPD-A33-R4: Document every breach, including those not notified, with the facts, effects and measures taken.

guidance: Guidelines 9/2022 on personal data breach notification

RGPD-A34.title: Communication of a breach to data subjects
RGPD-A34.statement: Where the breach is likely to result in a high risk to rights and freedoms, inform the data subjects without undue delay, in clear and plain language. Encryption rendering the data unintelligible exempts from this communication.

requirements.RGPD-A34-R1: Assess whether the risk to data subjects is high.
requirements.RGPD-A34-R2: Communicate the nature of the breach, the likely consequences and the measures taken.
requirements.RGPD-A34-R3: Use a public communication where individual notice would involve disproportionate effort.

RGPD-A34.deadline: Without undue delay once a high risk is established
evidence: Templates for communicating with data subjects

RGPD-A35.title: Data protection impact assessment
RGPD-A35.statement: Carry out an impact assessment before any processing likely to result in a high risk, notably systematic evaluation, large-scale processing of sensitive data, or large-scale systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area.

requirements.RGPD-A35-R1: Identify processing requiring an impact assessment, in light of the supervisory authority's list.
requirements.RGPD-A35-R2: Describe the processing, assess necessity and proportionality, evaluate risks and define measures.
requirements.RGPD-A35-R3: Seek the data protection officer's advice where there is one.
requirements.RGPD-A35-R4: Review the assessment when the risk changes.

evidence: List of processing subject to assessment
guidance: PIA software and impact assessment method

RGPD-A36.title: Prior consultation of the supervisory authority
RGPD-A36.statement: Where the impact assessment concludes that a high residual risk cannot be mitigated, consult the supervisory authority before starting the processing. The authority has eight weeks, extendable by six.

requirements.RGPD-A36-R1: Identify high residual risks at the end of the impact assessment.
requirements.RGPD-A36-R2: Refer to the authority and suspend implementation until it replies.

RGPD-A36.deadline: Before implementation, reply within 8 weeks extendable by 6
evidence: Referrals to the authority and replies received

RGPD-A37-39.chapter: Chapter IV, Section 4: Data protection officer
RGPD-A37-39.title: Designation and tasks of the data protection officer
RGPD-A37-39.statement: Designate a DPO where the organisation is a public authority, or where its core activities involve regular and systematic monitoring on a large scale, or large-scale processing of sensitive data. The DPO must be involved in all data protection matters and receive no instructions on how to carry out their tasks.

requirements.RGPD-A37-R1: Decide and document whether or not to designate a DPO.
requirements.RGPD-A37-R2: Publish the DPO's contact details and communicate them to the supervisory authority.
requirements.RGPD-A37-R3: Guarantee independence, absence of conflict of interest and reporting to the highest level.
requirements.RGPD-A37-R4: Give the DPO the resources needed to carry out their tasks.

RGPD-A37-39.deadline: Designation declared to the CNIL, ongoing role

RGPD-A40-43.chapter: Chapter IV, Section 5: Codes of conduct and certification
RGPD-A40-43.title: Codes of conduct and certification
RGPD-A40-43.statement: Adhering to an approved code of conduct or obtaining an approved certification is an element for demonstrating compliance. These schemes are optional but can be relied on in an inspection.

requirements.RGPD-A40-R1: Assess the relevance of an approved sectoral code of conduct.
requirements.RGPD-A40-R2: Where applicable, maintain the certification and submit to the body's monitoring.

evidence: Proof of adherence or valid certificate

RGPD-A44-49.chapter: Chapter V: Transfers to third countries
RGPD-A44-49.title: Transfers outside the European Union
RGPD-A44-49.statement: Only transfer data outside the Union on the basis of an adequacy decision, appropriate safeguards or, failing that, an Article 49 derogation. Since the Schrems II judgment, appropriate safeguards must be supplemented by a transfer impact assessment.

requirements.RGPD-A44-R1: Map outgoing flows, including remote access from a third country.
requirements.RGPD-A44-R2: Identify the basis for each transfer: adequacy, standard clauses, binding corporate rules, derogation.
requirements.RGPD-A44-R3: Carry out a transfer impact assessment evaluating the law of the destination country.
requirements.RGPD-A44-R4: Put in place the necessary supplementary technical or contractual measures.

RGPD-A44-49.deadline: Before any transfer, with periodic review

RGPD-A83.chapter: Chapter VIII: Remedies, liability and penalties
RGPD-A83.title: General conditions for administrative fines
RGPD-A83.statement: Know the two penalty tiers and the eleven adjustment criteria, to assess real exposure. Security measures, cooperation with the authority and certifications are expressly listed as mitigating circumstances.

requirements.RGPD-A83-R1: Identify the tier applicable to each category of breach.
requirements.RGPD-A83-R2: Document the elements constituting mitigating circumstances.

RGPD-A83.deadline: Scoping element, not an obligation in itself
